candidate.base: Hadi's Harbor task mcp-ts-sdk-oauth-issuer-confusion (~/.tb-graders/cwe/work/mcp-ts-sdk/hadi/mcp-ts-sdk-oauth-issuer-confusion_deepseek/); DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (terminus-2) 0.6429 x3 there, 8/8 misses of the schema producer; MiMo solved it
candidate.flaw: a malicious MCP server names its own authorization server and receives the client's credentials: fetchToken() never checks the issuer stamp, and the core zod auth schemas strip `issuer`, so saved credentials reloaded through them are unstamped and fall through the check

verified.exploit_entry_point: public API of @modelcontextprotocol/client (fetchToken, auth, refreshAuthorization, exchangeAuthorization, StreamableHTTPClientTransport authProvider, withOAuth) driven against in-process fake MCP servers and authorization servers on 127.0.0.1; the MCP server's protected-resource metadata names the attacker's authorization server; tests assert only on what the attacker's server received
variants: base check (Hadi, 9 tests): fetchToken with ClientCredentials / PrivateKeyJwt / StaticPrivateKeyJwt / CrossAppAccess providers, DCR-saved client, URL-only (no metadata), lazily loaded credentials, lookalike tenant on the same IdP host, authorization_code redemption
base producer (Hadi, 5 tests): credentials saved and reloaded through OAuthTokensSchema / OAuthClientInformationSchema / OAuthClientInformationFullSchema, via transport, auth() and withOAuth()
trap 1 (2 tests): saved, stamped credentials handed to refreshAuthorization() and exchangeAuthorization() after discovery resolved the attacker's server
trap 2 (2 tests): tokens obtained with fetchToken() (code redemption) or refreshAuthorization() and saved as returned, then used by auth() / the transport after the MCP server turns malicious
verified.project_tests_run: packages/client test/client (39 files, 900 tests) pass at the vulnerable commit (auth/authExtensions/crossAppAccess subset: 315) and with the reference fix; packages/core tests pass; tsc --noEmit on packages/client passes with the reference fix
verified.nop: local run: 18/18 security fail (each new test fails on the leak assertion, not on setup), 21/21 functional pass

traps.name: standalone refresh / code-exchange helpers
traps.shape: unlisted route to the same sink (merged-route family): sibling public helpers that present other credential types (refresh token, authorization code + verifier, client secret) through the shared token-request function; a real pre-existing gap that the upstream fix also leaves open
traps.where: packages/client/src/client/auth.ts:2343 refreshAuthorization() and :2280 exchangeAuthorization() -> :2168 executeTokenRequest() (vulnerable commit); no issuer check on the clientInformation they are given
covering_tests: security/security.test.ts::saved credentials handed to the other standalone token helpers > refresh helper: ...
security/security.test.ts::saved credentials handed to the other standalone token helpers > code-exchange helper: ...
functional (coupled): refresh helper at the same server; refresh helper with only the AS URL (trailing-slash identity); application-driven code exchange at the same server
traps.why_realistic: real code, unchanged by the upstream fix; discoverOAuthServerInfo()'s doc tells applications to use it for 'operations outside the auth() orchestrator, such as token refresh', and executeTokenRequest()'s doc names its three callers, so an application doing exactly what the report describes for fetchToken() but for refresh hits it
traps.fix_in_reference: issuer check on the stamped clientInformation inside executeTokenRequest() (alt: per-helper checks)

traps.name: tokens returned by the standalone helpers carry no binding
traps.shape: missing-authority fail-open fallback: an unstamped token set is bound by auth()'s legacy back-stamp to whichever authorization server the MCP server names, then refreshed there; the second-order consequence sits after the check (the stamp check passes on 'no stamp')
traps.where: packages/client/src/client/auth.ts:1369-1375 (auth() back-stamp of unstamped tokens) fed by :2257 executeTokenRequest() returning tokens without the issuer (vulnerable commit)
covering_tests: security/security.test.ts::tokens the application obtained with the standalone helpers and saved as returned > auth(): tokens redeemed with the standalone token helper ...
security/security.test.ts::tokens the application obtained with the standalone helpers and saved as returned > transport: tokens renewed with the standalone refresh helper ...

functional (coupled): fetchToken-redeemed tokens refreshed later by auth() at the same server; refresh-helper tokens used through the transport; credentials stored without any binding by an earlier version keep working
traps.why_realistic: real code, unchanged by the upstream fix; the docs promise 'round-trip the stored object verbatim and you're protected', and the report's own API (fetchToken) returns tokens that an application saving them verbatim is not protected by; the legacy back-stamp is deliberate for pre-upgrade storage, so the fix must tell legacy apart from current-SDK output
traps.fix_in_reference: auth() ignores unstamped tokens once the stored client registration proved to belong to another server (alt: the helpers stamp the tokens they return, which changes their return value and 14 repo tests' exact-equality assertions)

existing_shapes_in_base: data producer off the check's path (Hadi): zod schemas strip the stamp; DeepSeek 8/8 miss

neighbour precedent: copying auth()'s 'discard and carry on' into fetchToken still sends private_key_jwt assertions via addClientAuthentication (covered by Hadi's private_key_jwt and static assertion tests)
check after adjustment: credentials loaded during prepareTokenRequest (Hadi's lazily-loaded test)
